transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-27
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Agenda: renewal check-in, capacity uplift, EU private/on-prem pilot pathway, contract terms and next steps
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Ethan (Fjord Head of AI), Priya (Fjord Platform Eng), Alicia (Fjord Procurement)
---
Summary: Quick renewal check: Fjord is interested in extending commitment for 12 months, adding an EU private node (on-prem style) and reserve burst for holiday season. They want clarity on latency SLOs, KMS integration, SOC2 evidence, and a short private pilot to validate throughput before signing.
Topics: renewal sizing, private deployment topology, KMS/HSM options, benchmarking plan, procurement timings, fallback to hosted endpoints during pilot
---
Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. quick check, can you hear me ok?
[00:03] Ethan: yeah loud and clear, thanks Maya.
[00:06] Priya: we're good. Alicia's on too, just on mute.
[00:09] Maya: perfect. so high level today, we wanted to run through your renewal window, the proposed capacity bump, and the eu private node proposal. Jonah's here to answer the technicals.
[00:20] Jonah: hi all. i'll try to keep the deep stuff light unless you want details.
[00:24] Ethan: sounds good. quick context — we've been running redwood hosted for our chat flows and embeddings, production since march, volume's grown ~3x, and we need better tail latency for european customers and tighter data controls.
[00:38] Maya: got it. when you say tail latency what numbers are you seeing today?
[00:42] Ethan: p95 right now around 420 to 480ms for short chat requests; during peak windows it spikes to ~700ms. that's with hosted gen model. embeddings are fine.
[00:53] Jonah: that tracks with the throughput we've seen; burst windows are stressing the shared pools. dedicated or private edge can reduce the p95 but depends on model size, batching, and KV cache warmness.
[01:06] Priya: can you remind us the difference in guarantees if we go dedicated vs private onprem? and the cost delta?
[01:12] Maya: sure. dedicated (reserved capacity) gives you predictable throughput and an SLA on uptime; private (eu onprem node) gives you network isolation, you control the VPC and KMS, and reduces egress concerns — cost is higher because of infra+support and onboarding. i'll send a side-by-side after this.
[01:28] Alicia: procurement question — do you have a standard amendment for adding capacity mid-term or is this a new contract? we need PO language.
[01:35] Maya: we can do an amendment to the existing agreement; i'll put the exact PO wording in the quote.
[01:39] Ethan: timeline is tight — we want the private pilot validated before black friday (so mid-nov testing ideally) because we expect another 2.5x spike.
[01:50] Jonah: that's doable. for pilot we'd provision an eu private node in your VPC (or on-prem VM cluster) with a small dedicated pool and run a 72-hour soak with your trace. we instrument latency histograms and KV cache hit rates.
[02:03] Priya: what about KMS? we use an HSM-backed key with our provider — can redwood plug into our KMS for model keys and token encryption?
[02:12] Jonah: yes, we support customer-managed keys. for private nodes we can integrate with your cloud KMS or a transit HSM; we'd do key escrow and CMKs — we'll surface the exact flow in the security packet.
[02:23] Ethan: and audit logs? we need full request/response audit trails for compliance, retention 90 days, and SSO with SAML.
[02:31] Maya: we have audit logs and RBAC integration; for private deployment we can forward logs to your SIEM and set retention policy. i'm noting that as a must-have for the pilot.
[02:40] Alicia: ok procurement milestone — when do we need to sign to have provisioning for holiday traffic?
[02:45] Maya: if we sign by 2026-11-08, we can queue provisioning to hit the mid-nov pilot window; otherwise it slips into december.
[02:53] Ethan: that's tight but possible. pricing — are you offering a burst buffer? we don't want to overcommit monthly if the seasonal spikes are short.
[03:02] Maya: yes, we can structure a base commit plus a burst tier. typical is base commit + 20% burst at a higher per-token rate; we'll show blended unit economics.
[03:12] Priya: technical question for Jonah — for the onprem node, how does KV cache work? do we get prefix caching between instances?
[03:19] Jonah: good question. the KV cache is local to the node; we support shared cache if you run multiple collocated GPUs with our runtime in the same VPC subnet — it keeps cache warm for session affinity. if you're doing strict on-prem airgap there are some limitations on cross-host eviction sync but we have strategies.
[03:37] Ethan: hmm okay, we need to avoid cold-starts for our high-value customers. any recommended config?
[03:42] Jonah: pre-warming with a small synthetic traffic generator and sticky routing during the spike window usually gets p95 down 150–200ms. also quantization profile helps reduce latency for medium-size models.
[03:53] Priya: will quantization affect output quality for our customer-facing prompts? we've seen hallucinations at aggressive q4 in other stacks.
[03:59] Jonah: we'll run evals on your prompt set as part of the pilot. Redwood Optimize recommends safe quant profiles — usually q8 or int8 with per-layer shims to preserve logits. we'll include a quality baseline.
[04:12] Alicia: procurement again — what's the SLA if we run the private node? you said dedicated has an SLA; private onprem is more... how does that work?
[04:20] Maya: private nodes have a combined SLA for the control plane if you're on our managed private option; if fully on-prem self-hosted, SLA is limited to the control plane availability and support response times. we'll detail options in the appendix.
[04:33] Ethan: i want to bring up a competitor touchpoint — we ran a quick eval with CloudAI Services; they offered lower list price but didn't have the private edge playbook or KV cache strategy we need.
[04:44] Maya: we often see that — our differentiation is the production tooling and rollout controls.
[04:49] Priya: for the pilot we'll need a runbook: network ports, IAM roles, cert rotation, and a checklist for KMS. can you produce that?
[04:57] Jonah: yes, i'll draft a private-edge runbook and include firewall rules, NATS endpoints, and example kube manifests if you're on cluster.
[05:07] Ethan: great. will you also include a sample cost model for different traffic shapes?
[05:11] Maya: yes i'll include a spreadsheet with base commit, burst, and a blended per-10k-token column for three traffic profiles.
[05:18] Alicia: legal question — do you require data residency clauses for EU onprem? we need clause language for our legal counsel.
[05:25] Maya: we can include an EU data residency addendum, and for onprem the data never leaves your VPC — we'll put that in writing.
[05:31] Priya: we have one more technical ask — can the private node talk to our internal retriever service? we host vector DB in eu-central.
[05:37] Jonah: yes, long as network egress is allowed; recommended pattern is private peering with strict ACLs. we'll run a connectivity test during onboarding.
[05:45] Ethan: ok, recap from our side: we want a 12-month extension, base commit roughly 60% above current, plus a 20% burst for holiday. EU private pilot before black friday.
[05:56] Maya: sounds right. i'll put together the formal amendment and quote reflecting that.
[06:00] Alicia: procurement will need the invoice and PO-ready contract clauses — can you send them once quote is updated?
[06:06] Maya: yes, i'll bundle pricing, PO language, and the security packet.
[06:09] Priya: timeline — can Jonah kick off the onboarding checklist as soon as we sign?
[06:13] Jonah: absolutely. pilot playbook and runbook will be ready within 7 business days of sign. we'll also request your trace file for the 72-hour soak.
[06:22] Ethan: one thing — can we include an automatic fallback to hosted endpoints if private node experiences overload? we want graceful degradation.
[06:29] Jonah: yes, smart routing policy can failover to hosted model variant; we can set per-route fallbacks and rate limits.
[06:34] Priya: ok that's good. any blockers from Redwood side?
[06:37] Maya: none. main blockers are the procurement sign date and you providing trace and KMS details.
[06:43] Alicia: procurement target is to review by 2026-11-10 and sign by 2026-11-08 if possible, i'll confirm internally.
[06:50] Maya: perfect. next steps: i'll send quote + amendment + security packet by 2026-11-03; Jonah will send private runbook by 2026-11-10; Ethan and Priya to share traces and KMS info by 2026-11-05.
[06:59] Ethan: thanks everyone.
[07:01] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up in thread and book the kickoff meeting for the pilot.
